name: Ila
occupation: Former Scribe of the Akshapatala (Royal Accounts & Records Office) / Unassigned — stricken from civic rank
bloodline: Formerly of the Vishvamitra gotra scribal lineage (Xami division), now struck from the rolls
residence: An abandoned scribe's quarter near the old record-house, at the edge of the village bordering the Shalavana
personality: never fully trusts any single explanation
notices what people avoid more than what they say
daily_routine: copying old records from memory onto palm-leaf strips in her own cipher
observing movement through the market street and administrative quarter from a distance
rarely entering the central plaza unless necessary
collecting discarded record-fragments and broken seals
monitoring changes in temple and administrative behavior
avoiding direct interaction unless approached first

goals.hidden_goal: Preserve a complete reconstruction of the Akshapatala's records from before the ash-year, and map where the official history diverges from what still stands in stone and timber
goals.deep_goal: Understand why certain records were systematically removed rather than lost

beliefs: Absence of records is itself meaningful
Systems erase what they fear will be reinterpreted
Memory exists in both people and structures
The administration is not hiding the truth — it is managing it
